html:
The first modern Olympic Games, held in Athens in April 1896. Athletes from 14 nations took part.

The idea came from a French educator, Pierre de Coubertin, who wanted to revive the ancient Olympic Games of Greece as an international festival of sport and peace. He founded the International Olympic Committee in Paris in 1894, and Athens was chosen to host the first games, as a tribute to their origin.

The main venue was the ancient Panathenaic Stadium, rebuilt in marble for the occasion. About 240 athletes competed, all men, in sports such as athletics, cycling, fencing, gymnastics, shooting, swimming, tennis, weightlifting and wrestling. The American James Connolly, in the triple jump, became the first modern Olympic champion.

The highlight for the hosts was the new marathon race, based on the legend of a runner from Marathon to Athens. A Greek water carrier, Spyridon Louis, won it, to huge celebration.

The games were a success, and the Olympics have since been held every four years, except in the World wars.
sum: The first modern Olympic Games, held in Athens in April 1896. Athletes from 14 nations took part.
